subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should the repository trust these exact new GitHub Action revisions in workflows that handle credentials, security scans, agent execution, automation tokens, and release publishing?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow, but approving newly downloaded executable code with access to secrets and write-capable workflows is a security-owner decision that CI cannot settle; the Codex-specific source gate also requires direct maintainer inspection.

options.title: Approve after trust review
options.body: Have secops and the relevant workflow owner inspect the upstream changes, complete the direct Codex-source check, and merge after exact-head checks are acceptable.

options.title: Split privileged updates
options.body: Land low-privilege setup-action pins separately and hold token, Codex, CodeQL, Docker login, and publishing action updates for narrower review.

recommendation.title: Approve after trust review
recommendation.body: Have secops and the relevant workflow owner inspect the upstream changes, complete the direct Codex-source check, and merge after exact-head checks are acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS explicitly assigns this team to multiple security-sensitive workflows changed by the PR.
